text: Water drops are falling from a nozzle of a shower onto the floor, from a height of 9.8 m. The drops fall at a regular interval of time. When the first drop strikes the floor, at that instant, the third drop begins to fall. Locate the position of second drop from the floor when the first drop strikes the floor.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

H = $\frac{1}{2}gt^{2}$

$\frac{9.8\times 2}{9.8}$ $= t^{2}$

t = $\sqrt{2}$ sec

$\Delta$t : time interval between drops

h = $\frac{1}{2}$g($\sqrt{2}$ $-$ $\Deltat)^{2}$

$\Delta$t = $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

h = $\frac{1}{2}$g$\left (\sqrt{2}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\times 9.8\times \frac{1}{2}=\frac{9.8}{4}=2.45$ m

H $-$ h = 9.8 $-$ 2.45

= 7.35 m

text:
A constant magnetic field of 1T is applied in the x > 0 region. A metallic circular ring of radius 1m is moving with a constant velocity of 1 m/s along the x-axis. At t = 0s, the centre of O of the ring is at x = $-$1m. What will be the value of the induced emf in the ring at t = 1s? (Assume the velocity of the ring does not change.)


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The field $B=1\text{T}$ fills the hatched region $x>0$ and is normal to the plane of the ring; $R=1\text{m}$, $v=1\text{m s}^{-1}$.

At $t=1\text{s}$ the centre O has moved from $x=-1\text{m}$ to $x=0$, so the right half of the ring is in the field and the boundary $x=0$ cuts the ring along a diameter.

The area of the ring inside the field then grows at the rate $\dfrac{dA}{dt}=(\text{chord on}x=0)\times v=2Rv$, so

$ε=B\dfrac{dA}{dt}=B(2R)v=1\times 2\times 1=2\text{V}$

The effective length is this chord $2R$ joining the ends of the arc inside the field, not the arc length $πR$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift

text: A mass of 50 kg is placed at the centre of a uniform spherical shell of mass 100 kg and radius 50 m. If the gravitational potential at a point, 25 m from the centre is V kg/m. The value of V is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The point A at $r=25\text{m}$ lies inside the shell of radius $R=50\text{m}$, where the potential due to the shell is constant and equal to its surface value $-\dfrac{GM_{2}}{R}$.


[IMG]

Potential at A due to the point mass $M_{1}=50\text{kg}$ at the centre:

$V_{1}=-\dfrac{GM_{1}}{r}=-\dfrac{50G}{25}=-2G$

Potential at A due to the shell of mass $M_{2}=100\text{kg}$:

$V_{2}=-\dfrac{GM_{2}}{R}=-\dfrac{100G}{50}=-2G$

Potentials add as scalars:

$V=V_{1}+V_{2}=-4G$

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: Two simple harmonic motion, are represented by the equations $y_{1}=10\sin \left (3πt+\frac{π}{3}\right )$ $y_{2}=5(\sin 3πt+\sqrt{3}\cos 3πt)$ Ratio of amplitude of $y_{1}$ to $y_{2} = x$ : 1. The value of x is $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$y_{1}=10\sin \left (3πt+\frac{π}{3}\right )$ $\Rightarrow$ Amplitude = 10

$y_{2}=5(\sin 3πt+\sqrt{3}\cos 3πt)$

$y_{2}=10\left (\frac{1}{2}\sin 3πt+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos 3πt\right )$

$y_{2}=10\left (\cos \frac{π}{3}\sin 3πt+\sin \frac{π}{3}\cos 3πt\right )$

$y_{2}=10\left (3πt+\frac{π}{3}\right )$ $\Rightarrow$ Amplitude = 10

So ratio of amplitudes = $\frac{10}{10}$ = 1

solution.body:
When unregulated voltage is 14 V voltage across zener diode must be 10 V. So potential difference across resistor $\DeltaV_{Rs} = 4V$

text:
A bullet of 10 g, moving with velocity v, collides head-on with the stationary bob of a pendulum and recoils with velocity 100 m/s. The length of the pendulum is 0.5 m and mass of the bob is 1 kg. The minimum value of $v = ____________ m/s$ so that the pendulum describes a circle. (Assume the string to be inextensible and $g = 10 m/s^{2})$


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the bob to complete the vertical circle, the tension at the top may just vanish, so the minimum speed there is $\sqrt{gl}$; energy conservation from the lowest point to the top ($2l$ higher) gives the minimum speed at the lowest point:

$v_{b}^{2}=gl+4gl=5gl\Rightarrow v_{b}=\sqrt{5\times 10\times 0.5}=5\text{m s}^{-1}$

Momentum is conserved in the collision. Taking the bullet's initial direction as positive, the recoiling bullet has velocity $-100\text{m s}^{-1}$ ($m=0.01$ kg, $M=1$ kg):

$0.01v=1\times 5+0.01\times (-100)$

$0.01v=5-1=4\Rightarrow v=400\text{m s}^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 400.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift

text: A tuning fork is vibrating at 250 Hz. The length of the shortest closed organ pipe that will resonate with the tuning fork will be $__________ cm. ($Take speed of sound in air as $340 ms^{-1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

$\frac{λ}{4}$ = l $\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = 4l 

f = $\frac{V}{λ}=\frac{V}{4l}$

$\Rightarrow$ 250 = $\frac{340}{4l}$

$\Rightarrow$ l = $\frac{34}{4\times 25}$ = 0.34 m

l = 34 cm
